title: Number of Students Allowed to Return to School for Support with Technology-based Learning during COVID-19 Circuit Breaker Period
what_it_is: Number of Students Allowed to Return to School for Support with Technology-based Learning during COVID-19 Circuit Breaker Period

sections.label: Full HBL participation rate
sections.summary: Participation in full HBL averaged 96% across the levels.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Participation in full HBL was high, averaging 96% across the levels.

sections.label: Loaned computing and Internet devices
sections.summary: Schools have loaned over 20,000 computing devices and 1,600 Internet-enabling devices, with some corporate support.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: To support this group, schools have loaned out more than 20,000 computing devices and 1,600 Internet-enabling devices to date, with some support from corporates.

sections.label: Students returning to school daily
sections.summary: About 3,300 Primary and 700 Secondary students returned to school daily, and parental requests were met for genuine needs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Over the full HBL period, about 3,300 Primary school students and 700 Secondary school students returned to school daily for one or more of the above reasons.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Requests from parents for their children to return to school were met, as long as there were genuine needs.

sections.label: Adjustments then stabilisation over weeks
sections.summary: The first week involved many adjustments and learning, but by the fourth week things had more or less stabilised.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, I would say that the initial period – certainly, the first week – there was quite a lot of adjustments that had to take place and learning on both sides.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But a couple of weeks on and now we are at the fourth week, things have more or less stabilised.

sections.label: MOE feedback and online learning balance
sections.summary: MOE is reviewing feedback and learnings, including that online lesson preparation differs from face-to-face and needs the right balance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: MOE is already beginning to look at some of the feedback and the learnings that we have derived from this.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: One of the pieces of feedback that has come, for example, is that teachers have said that the preparation of the lesson plans for online learning or learning through virtual platforms, is very different from face-to-face learning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And the way you prepare the resources that you use and how you package it together is different.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: They are also looking at the right balance because after awhile, if it is only pure online learning, children get bored.
